items.title: Ruthie Foster interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, February 28, 2023
items.q: I had a guitar player, drummer, bass player, and I think Cyd, Cyd Cassone was on percussion that night.

ctx.x: It was a number of years ago when I saw you on Austin City Limits, not the most recent time but it was a small group. You had a woman who provided vocal harmonies and some percussion. And I was hooked from the get-go. It was late at night, I got home from a gig and I was just sort of winding down. And again, serendipity, I landed on this. And if I can recall the feeling it just seemed that even though the instrumentation was sparse that’s all that was required at that time.

Yeah. I think that has a lot to do with — keeping the instrumentation sparse was important for me. It had a lot to do with my wanting to keep the song up front. It’s about the song for me, and I am a songwriter. I like to call myself a singer, but I love to think that I’m a songwriter first and that’s important for instrumentation on stage. And yeah, I remember that night. I had a guitar player, drummer, bass player, and I think Cyd, Cyd Cassone was on percussion that night. Yeah, we kept it pretty simple. Pretty…
It seems that you have a fairly well defined vision for your music and I read this bit about you turning down a deal with Atlantic Records. Is that correct?
